insert.title: How BTreeMap::insert works
insert.description: Like HashMap::insert, but the keys are always kept in sorted order.

slides.caption: A BTreeMap keeps its keys sorted, so iterating always gives them in order.
Choose BTreeMap when you need sorted keys or ranges; HashMap is usually faster for plain lookups.

range.title: How BTreeMap::range works
range.description: Iterates over the entries whose keys fall in a range, in order.

slides.caption: Because the keys are sorted, range can jump straight to the first key >= 2.

Great for time ranges, scores between two values, or "everything after this key".

first_key_value.title: How BTreeMap::first_key_value works
first_key_value.description: The entry with the smallest key.

btreeset-insert.description: A set that keeps its values sorted.

push_front.title: How VecDeque::push_front works
push_front.description: Adds an item at the front, without shifting the others.

slides.caption: A VecDeque is a ring buffer: it can grow at the front as cheaply as at the back.
2 and 3 stay where they are in memory.
1 is written in front of them, without moving anything.

pop_front.title: How VecDeque::pop_front works
pop_front.description: Removes the first item: a queue, first in, first out.

slides.caption: Items are added at the back with push_back and taken from the front with pop_front.
1 was added first, so it leaves first.
2 is now at the front, ready to be next.
push_back + pop_front is a queue (first in, first out); push_back + pop_back is a stack.

push_back.title: How VecDeque::push_back works
push_back.description: Adds an item at the back.

slides.caption: push_back appends at the end of the queue.

push.title: How BinaryHeap::push works
push.description: Adds a value; the largest value is always on top.

pop.title: How BinaryHeap::pop works
pop.description: Removes and returns the largest value.

slides.caption: Each pop takes the current largest value off the top; the next largest takes its place.
Then 3. One more pop would give None.

pop_back takes the item at the back of the deque.

A VecDeque can be used from both ends, as a queue or as a stack.

peek.title: How BinaryHeap::peek works

get.title: How BTreeMap::get works

pop_first.title: How BTreeMap::pop_first works

last_key_value.title: How BTreeMap::last_key_value works

entry.title: How BTreeMap::entry works

front.title: How VecDeque::front works

btree_occupied-remove.title: How BTreeMap OccupiedEntry::remove works
btree_occupied-remove.description: Removes the entry and returns its value.

slides.caption: Decide based on the value, then remove, with one lookup.

remove_entry.title: How BTreeMap OccupiedEntry::remove_entry works
remove_entry.description: Removes the entry and returns both the key and the value.

slides.caption: Useful when the key is an owned String you want to reuse.
The map is one entry smaller.

btree_vacant-insert.title: How BTreeMap VacantEntry::insert works
btree_vacant-insert.description: Fills the missing key and returns &mut to the new value.

slides.caption: Only reached when the key did not exist.
or_insert is the shortcut for this pattern.

btree_vacant-key.title: How BTreeMap VacantEntry::key works
btree_vacant-key.description: The key that would be inserted.

slides.caption: Look at the key before deciding to insert.
Nothing has been inserted at this point.

into_key.title: How BTreeMap VacantEntry::into_key works
into_key.description: Gives the key back without inserting.

slides.caption: entry() took ownership of the key; into_key returns it.
Avoids cloning an expensive key just to look.

btree_vacant-insert_entry.title: How BTreeMap VacantEntry::insert_entry works
btree_vacant-insert_entry.description: Inserts the value and returns an OccupiedEntry for it.

slides.caption: Unlike insert, you get an entry back instead of a plain reference.
The occupied entry knows key and value.
Handy when you may want to remove it again.

get_key_value.title: How BTreeMap::get_key_value works
get_key_value.description: The stored key and its value.

slides.caption: Returns the key as stored in the map, not the one you passed.
Useful when equal keys can still differ (e.g. different capitalisation rules).

iter_mut.title: How BTreeMap::iter_mut works
iter_mut.description: Visits every entry in key order with a mutable value.

slides.caption: values_mut if you do not need the keys.

btreemap-remove_entry.title: How BTreeMap::remove_entry works
btreemap-remove_entry.description: Removes a key and returns both the stored key and the value.

slides.caption: None if the key is missing.

extract_if.title: How BTreeMap::extract_if works
extract_if.description: Removes entries in a key range that pass a test, and gives them to you.

slides.caption: The range (.. means all) limits which keys are looked at.
Keys 1 and 3 pass: moved out, in order.
retain keeps the passing entries instead.

btreeset-get.title: How BTreeSet::get works
btreeset-get.description: A reference to the stored value equal to the one given.

slides.caption: contains says yes or no; get returns the element.

is_disjoint.title: How BTreeSet::is_disjoint works
is_disjoint.description: true if the two sets have nothing in common.

slides.caption: Disjoint means the intersection is empty.
Check schedules or ID ranges for overlaps.

is_superset.title: How BTreeSet::is_superset works
is_superset.description: true if this set contains every value of the other.

slides.caption: Every element of b must be in a.

replace.title: How BTreeSet::replace works
replace.description: Inserts a value, replacing an equal one, and returns the old one.

slides.caption: insert keeps the old element; replace swaps it out.
Matters when equal values still carry different data.

take.title: How BTreeSet::take works
take.description: Removes a value and returns it.

slides.caption: remove returns a bool; take returns the owned value.
None if the value was not there.

btreeset-extract_if.title: How BTreeSet::extract_if works
btreeset-extract_if.description: Removes values in a range that pass a test, and gives them to you.

slides.caption: The removed values come out in sorted order.
retain keeps the passing values instead.

vecdeque-iter_mut.title: How VecDeque::iter_mut works
vecdeque-iter_mut.description: Visits every element front to back, mutably.

slides.caption: Works even when the ring buffer wraps around.

as_mut_slices.title: How VecDeque::as_mut_slices works
as_mut_slices.description: The contents as two mutable slices (the ring buffer may wrap).

slides.caption: Together the two slices hold every element in order.
make_contiguous gives a single slice instead.

binary_search_by.title: How VecDeque::binary_search_by works
binary_search_by.description: Binary search in a sorted deque with your own comparison.

slides.caption: The closure compares each probed element with the target.
Err(i) tells where to insert to keep order.

binary_search_by_key.title: How VecDeque::binary_search_by_key works
binary_search_by_key.description: Binary search on a key extracted from each element.

slides.caption: The deque must be sorted by that key.

partition_point.title: How VecDeque::partition_point works
partition_point.description: The index of the first element for which the test becomes false.

slides.caption: The deque must be split: all trues first, then all falses.
8 is the first that is not: index 3.
A binary search, so it is fast on big deques.

pop_front_if.title: How VecDeque::pop_front_if works
pop_front_if.description: Removes the front element only if it passes a test.

slides.caption: Handy to drain items that are ready, stopping at the first that is not.
pop_back_if works at the other end.

pop_back_if.title: How VecDeque::pop_back_if works
pop_back_if.description: Removes the back element only if it passes a test.

slides.caption: Looks at the last element first.

vecdeque-range_mut.title: How VecDeque::range_mut works
vecdeque-range_mut.description: Mutable access to a range of positions.

capacity.title: How VecDeque::capacity works
capacity.description: How many elements fit before the deque must grow.

slides.caption: len counts elements; capacity counts room.
Growing doubles the buffer, like Vec.

reserve.title: How VecDeque::reserve works
reserve.description: Makes room for at least n more elements.

slides.caption: One allocation now instead of several later.

reserve_exact.title: How VecDeque::reserve_exact works
reserve_exact.description: Reserves room for exactly n more elements.

slides.caption: Use it when the final size is known.
The allocator may still round up.
Useful after a queue was temporarily very full.

try_reserve.title: How VecDeque::try_reserve works
try_reserve.description: Reserves room, returning an error instead of aborting.

slides.caption: Asks for just enough room, and reports failure.
Vec and String have the same method.

resize_with.title: How VecDeque::resize_with works
resize_with.description: Grows or shrinks to a length, creating new elements with a closure.

title.text: let mut n = 1; q.resize_with(3, || { n += 1; n });

slides.caption: New elements are added at the back.
resize(len, value) clones one value instead.

retain_mut.title: How VecDeque::retain_mut works
retain_mut.description: Keeps elements that pass a test; the test may also change them.

slides.caption: Every element is visited once and may be changed before the decision.
retain only gets a shared reference.

swap_remove_back.title: How VecDeque::swap_remove_back works
swap_remove_back.description: Removes an element by moving the last element into its place.

slides.caption: No shifting: the back element fills the hole.
Use it when order does not matter.

swap_remove_front.title: How VecDeque::swap_remove_front works
swap_remove_front.description: Removes an element by moving the front element into its place.

slides.caption: The front element fills the hole.

binaryheap-with_capacity.title: How BinaryHeap::with_capacity works
binaryheap-with_capacity.description: An empty heap with room for n elements.

slides.caption: Avoids growth while the queue fills.

as_slice.title: How BinaryHeap::as_slice works
as_slice.description: The elements in internal heap order, as a slice.

slides.caption: The first element is always the maximum.
The buffer is shown as it is.

binaryheap-capacity.title: How BinaryHeap::capacity works
binaryheap-capacity.description: How many elements fit before the heap grows.

binaryheap-reserve.title: How BinaryHeap::reserve works
binaryheap-reserve.description: Makes room for at least n more elements.

binaryheap-reserve_exact.title: How BinaryHeap::reserve_exact works
binaryheap-reserve_exact.description: Reserves room for exactly n more elements.

slides.caption: The allocator may still round up.
After a burst of work, give memory back.

binaryheap-try_reserve.title: How BinaryHeap::try_reserve works
binaryheap-try_reserve.description: Reserves room, returning an error instead of aborting.

slides.caption: Same pattern on Vec and String.

peekmut-pop.title: How PeekMut::pop works
peekmut-pop.description: Removes the top element you are peeking at.

title.text: if let Some(top) = h.peek_mut() { if *top > 5 { PeekMut::pop(top); } }

slides.caption: Peek, check, and pop in one lookup.
It is popped; 4 is on top.
Useful for "pop while the top is ready".
Prefer Vec or VecDeque unless you need O(1) splitting and joining.

linkedlist-back.title: How LinkedList::back works
linkedlist-back.description: The last element, without removing it.

linkedlist-back_mut.title: How LinkedList::back_mut works
linkedlist-back_mut.description: A mutable reference to the last element.

linkedlist-front_mut.title: How LinkedList::front_mut works
linkedlist-front_mut.description: A mutable reference to the first element.

linkedlist-is_empty.title: How LinkedList::is_empty works
linkedlist-is_empty.description: true if the list has no elements.

slides.caption: Instant: the list keeps its length.
while let Some(x) = l.pop_front() avoids the check.
Each node is freed one by one.

linkedlist-iter.title: How LinkedList::iter works
linkedlist-iter.description: Visits elements from front to back by following the links.

linkedlist-iter_mut.title: How LinkedList::iter_mut works
linkedlist-iter_mut.description: Visits elements mutably from front to back.

slides.caption: Each node's value is lent mutably.
The links themselves cannot be changed this way.

linkedlist-split_off.title: How LinkedList::split_off works
linkedlist-split_off.description: Splits the list in two at an index.

slides.caption: Finding the index is O(n); the split itself just relinks.
append() joins lists back in O(1).

clone.title: How VecDeque::clone works
clone.description: A copy of the deque with clones of every element.

slides.caption: The copy is laid out contiguously.
clone_from can reuse an existing buffer.

btreemap-clone.title: How BTreeMap::clone works
btreemap-clone.description: A copy of the sorted map with clones of every entry.

slides.caption: The tree is copied node by node.

linkedlist-extend.title: How LinkedList::extend works
linkedlist-extend.description: Appends every item of an iterator to the end.

slides.caption: append() moves a whole list in O(1).

push_back_mut.title: How VecDeque::push_back_mut works
push_back_mut.description: Pushes to the back and returns a mutable reference.

slides.caption: Here the value is a String.

push_front_mut.title: How VecDeque::push_front_mut works
push_front_mut.description: Pushes to the front and returns a mutable reference.

insert_mut.title: How VecDeque::insert_mut works
insert_mut.description: Inserts at an index and returns a mutable reference.

linkedlist-push_back_mut.title: How LinkedList::push_back_mut works
linkedlist-push_back_mut.description: Appends a node and returns a mutable reference to its value.

linkedlist-push_front_mut.title: How LinkedList::push_front_mut works
linkedlist-push_front_mut.description: Prepends a node and returns a mutable reference to its value.

linkedlist-extract_if.title: How LinkedList::extract_if works
linkedlist-extract_if.description: Removes the nodes that pass a test and gives them to you.

slides.caption: retain keeps the passing nodes instead.
